text:
Predicates:
Contain(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Reads(x, y) ::: x reads book y.
Gains(x, y) ::: x gains knowledge from y.
Smarter(x) ::: x is smarter.
Premises:
∀x ∃y (Contain(y, x) ∧ Knowledge(x)) ::: Books contain tons of knowledge.
∀x ∀y (Reads(x, y) → Gains(x, Knowledge(y))) ::: When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge.
∀x (Gains(x, y) → Smarter(x)) ::: If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter.
Reads(Harry, Walden) ::: Harry read the book “Walden” by Henry Thoreau.
Conclusion:
Contain(Walden, Knowledge) ::: Walden contains knowledge.
